overview: The Towans are the long line of dunes stretching from the mouth of the Hayle estuary towards Gwithian, and below them runs a huge golden beach facing out across St Ives Bay. This is the Hayle end, with lifeguards in season, parking and cafés near the sand.
Hayle itself was once an important mining port and steam-engine-building town. Today the beach is the draw: so much space that even on a busy summer day you can walk off and find your own patch.

expect.title: Miles of sand
expect.text: A huge beach stretching north-east along the bay towards Gwithian and Godrevy.

expect.title: Dunes
expect.text: The dunes behind the beach are great for exploring, but keep to the paths to protect them.

expect.title: The estuary
expect.text: At the western end, the Hayle estuary separates the Towans from Porth Kidney Sands and Carbis Bay.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: Hayle is about seven miles north-east of Penzance.

week.text: A brilliant big-beach day, with room for games, walks and paddles. Combine it with Paradise Park in Hayle if the weather wobbles.

pairWith.why: the next stretch of sand towards Godrevy
a wildlife park with indoor play
a quiet beach across the estuary

tips: Keep children away from the estuary mouth, where currents can be strong.
